Heyho, I created an issue on Github for this, content in ticket is the same as here: https://github.com/madmanbeavisx/NarcoNet/issues/2

During testing, playing and testing I found some tweaks and maybe some of them are useful to be integrated by you

comments.author: Chani
comments.body_html:
Fair. My setup is a fika server as a docker container (so effectively a separate machine). And an actual separate machine that handles a fika headless raid server. Then my computer that I play the game on, and my friends with their computers to play the game on. My use case is I want the fika headless client to be excluded from syncing so it doesn’t get mods deleted or misconfigured.

If you don’t have a fika headless server (so when you go to host raids you do it from the same client that you’re playing on (most people do this) then you don’t need to exclude anything. The only reason for a separate machine running the fika headless server is to offload the CPU processing of all the AI and map mechanics so your machine can focus on playing the game.

If I understand your setup correctly, your fika server is on the same machine you’re playing the game on, and your client is playing and hosting at the same time, then yes Narco would work fine for you. When your friends connect to your machine it’d sync all your mods to them so they can play the same way you do without having to do any of the setup you had to do for your client.

comments.author: flir
comments.body_html:
Note: I release a more recent version see comment below for info

Hi all, I have fixed a few errors in this mod and made a release.

This contains a lot of fixes.

There were numerous race conditions, client side exclusions not respected during incremental sync … Hopefully this makes the mod useable :p

For the original authors: the source code is available here

Some changes you may not want to take in as I added CI builds for gitlab and you are using github. I also removed the Winforms dependency as it made it difficult to build in CI. This one I think is a good thing and you should keep as it allows building/testing and releasing from CI.

I added a nuget system to allow using the nugets from the CI build I refactored the references to use variables that can easily be changed and applied to all the refs (easier to move the refs places without editing hundreds of refs manually)

I tested it with a server hosted on Linux with the most excellent docker image from zhliau with Windows clients connecting to it and it works like a charm for my use case.

I am willing to continue helping if needed as a “sync mod” is vital to me. So if the project becomes unmaintained (no bugfix since nov 2025?) I am proposing to become a co-author and be allowed to push new releases.

For all the people having issue can you try this release and report if it corrects your issue ?

comments.author: FriedEngineer
comments.body_html:
Thanks for your work on this flir! v1.0.14 works better than 1.0.2 (which wouldn’t update files and ignored the exclusion list) and 1.0.13 (which crashed my linux backend).

With 1.0.14 I have encountered an issue with the client mod being super aggressive about deleting files created locally. The first time I ran it it annoying wiped my BepInEx/config. The first and every time after it also deletes BepInEx/plugis/SAIN/BotTypes.json, BepInEx/plugis/SAIN/Default Bot Config Values, and BepInEx/plugis/SAIN/Presets. After it deletes them, it instructs me to exit, which kills the client. However the SAIN mod recreates those files every time, so NarcoNetBut says they need to be deleted again on the next launch, in an endless loop. On my local client I just hit skip to get out of the loop and start playing. On the headless it sends it into an actual loop because the headless FIka client (correctly) accepts the changes automatically, so I had to remove NarcoNet from the headless client after it synced everything down on the first run.

Also thank you for the much expanded exclusion list for the headless fika client! There’s a few more mods I would like to request be added to that exclusion list:

  • BepInEx/plugins/acidphantasm-stattrack/ - this is disallowed explicitly by the headless client mod code so will stop the client from booting. https://github.com/project-fika/Fika-Headless/blob/79e81b8f179e1d126babe5128ea6cb929f967ad2/Fika.Headless/FikaHeadlessPlugin.cs#L419
  • BepInEx/plugins/HealingAutoCancel.dll - the client loads but I’ve found that it causes issues once the raid starts
  • BepInEx/plugins/InteractableExfilsAPI/ - this causes the client to crash right after the raid starts.

comments.author: asaguda
comments.body_html:
Is there any chance for this to get a config syncing option that works more like ModSync used to? With ModSync, I supplied my players with a small set of configs, anything we didn’t run as default, with curated changes. If the players then changed their local configs, ModSync did not overwrite them- Unless I changed a config on the server, which would then trigger another update of that specific config. This meant that I only needed the configs we don’t run as default on the server, and that personal preference changes had a common starting point and would be respected until I changed something on the server side.

This is the only thing missing for this to be a truly ‘set and forget’ experience for my group. A toggle to ignore client-side config changes unless the file has been modified on the server, or something like that. EDIT: Apparently, this is called ‘last modified wins’ in computer speak. The more you know?
